question: Audit the 89 FY2024 sponsor-years that itemise less than half of Part IX line 1 on Schedule I (suspected partial itemisation, $0.81bn DAF-weighted, 1.4 points of netted grants; largest Blackbaud Giving Fund, Omaha CF, Nevada CF): read each return's Schedule I Part I lines 2-3 recipient counts and any attachment, and classify the shortfall as sub-$5,000 gifts, attachment-only lists or parse loss
conclusion_affected: Allocation key for 1.4 of the 4.7 points of non-itemised domestic grants; recipient-share medians
rationale: The bounded allocation spreads these dollars pro rata because they are unlikely to be small gifts; if most are attachment-only lists, they belong with the non-itemising sponsors instead. Pooled shares barely move (≤0.1 point); medians move by up to 2 points between keys

question: Reconcile R5 netting with the line-level DAF-to-DAF drop: the numerator drops $9.45bn of DAF-weighted DAF-to-DAF Schedule I lines in FY2024 but R5 (central) nets $8.03bn from the denominator; identify which whitelisted recipients or caps account for the $1.42bn (2.4 points of netted grants) and whether those dollars reach DAF accounts or sponsors' non-DAF funds
conclusion_affected: Netted market total ($58.41bn); 2.4 of the 15.1 gap points; the upper sensitivity of the recipient share (+0.2 point)
rationale: This is the largest gap component that is neither foreign, small nor unitemised. It is treated as reaching no frame recipient (they are panel sponsors, excluded from the frame), but if R5 under-nets, the netted denominator is too high and coverage is understated

question: Adopt the re-weighted DAF share w2 = min(1, DAFRC corrected DAF grants / (Part IX line 1 + line 3)) in place of the cost-structure share in the recipient-share numerator, and propagate it to b40n1202-01 and b40n1202-b43n26 tables (it zeroes 129 default-weight sponsor-years with no DAFRC DAF grants, e.g. Campanile Foundation, Give2Asia, and raises UCLA Foundation and Stanford from near 0)
conclusion_affected: DAF weighting of non-top-50 sponsors; resolves P-B40N120201-02 (default weight of 1)
rationale: w2 puts numerator and netted denominator on the same DAFRC basis and removes the DAF-weighting haircut almost entirely (residual 0.13 point, 63 capped sponsor-years). Its effect on the pooled share is small (+0.03 point on 1h) but it fixes sponsor-level misweighting

question: Obtain recipient lists for the non-itemising sponsors from primary sources: BofA Charitable Gift Fund ($1.04bn raw FY2024 DAF grants), Renaissance Charitable Foundation ($0.72bn) and The Donors Fund ($0.55bn corrected) file Schedule I as attachments; check whether the IRS TEOS PDF image or the sponsor's own annual report lists grantees, and if so allocate those $2.6bn directly
conclusion_affected: 4.4 of the 15.1 gap points; the top-50 versus all-sponsor key choice
rationale: These dollars are allocated by the top-50 itemised pattern (central) or the all-sponsor pattern (bound). The two keys give nearly the same frame share (0.69 vs 0.68), so the pooled share is robust, but band and sector cuts are not tested

question: Calibrate the sub-$5,000 allocation key with an observed small-grant distribution: find FY2023-24 sponsors that itemise all grants, including those under $5,000, on Schedule I or in a public grant list (only $6.7m of lines under $5,000 are itemised in the panel), and compare their recipient-size mix for gifts under $5,000 with the under-$10,000 key
conclusion_affected: Recipient-share medians and the <$1m band (median 10.2% vs 11.9% between keys; <$1m pooled 22.1-23.3%)
rationale: Pooled shares are insensitive to the key (range 0.1 point), but medians and small-band shares depend on it; the under-$10,000 key is an analogue, not an observation

question: Replace the residual-scaled recipient shares in repo passages (b40n1202-01 §0 and §2.3, b40n12 §0, b40n1202-b43n26 §0, report §11.52) with the bounded allocation: 1h 9.2% (allocation range 9.1-9.2%, 95% CI about 8.2-10.2%) and 1h-1d-1e 13.7% (13.7-13.8%) on the committed frame, replacing 8.4-9.9% and 12.6-14.8%
conclusion_affected: Headline DAF share of recipient contributions
rationale: The residual 1/0.849 scaling assigns all 15.1 points pro rata; 3.0 points are foreign, 2.4 are DAF-to-DAF accounting and the rest reaches frame recipients at about the itemised rate, so the bounded figure sits in the lower third of the old range
